checks.note: Known deviation of about +2 %: the engine converges to 91.24 V (Richardson extrapolation, observed order 2.6, from 1, 0.5 and 0.25 m segments; Galerkin and collocation agree within 0.3 %). With 3.5-7 m segments it reproduces 86-89 V, so the published range is most likely under-resolved at the corner, where leakage current concentrates. Not an engine defect; pending confirmation of the programs' segmentation (IEEE 80-2013 Table H.5) or a fine-segment run in a commercial tool.

cases.description: IEEE 80 Annex B Exhibit 1: 60.96 m (200 ft) square, 5 x 5 conductors at 15.24 m, radius 5 mm at 0.5 m, nine 9.144 m rods (radius 6.35 mm) at the corners, mid-sides and centre; two-layer soil 300 ohm-m over 100 ohm-m, upper layer 4.572 m (15 ft)
assumptions: mesh voltage at the centre of the corner mesh (7.62, 7.62); step voltage 1 m diagonally outward from the grid corner

checks.note: Known deviation (-12 to -19 %), also unexplained by an independent solver (protectionpro BACKLOG: 'Exhibit 1 unexplained'). Without rods the engine gives 1.4112 ohm against 1.4102 ohm from that solver. With rods shortened to 4 m (not reaching the 100 ohm-m layer) it reproduces the published figures (1.357 ohm, 49.3 %, 17.3 %), so the EPRI result most likely did not model the 9.144 m rods penetrating the lower layer. Rods crossing the interface are validated by Annex H Grids 3-6. Informative only.
